items.answer: The AI Career Guidance App does not provide a percentage chance of getting placed at a top company. The readiness estimate is not a hiring probability or a guarantee. items.answer: No readiness estimate has been computed yet (the student can run it from the Readiness page). Improving SQL is important for the Data Analyst role, but it is not a guarantee of being hired. The app's readiness model shows that no estimate has been computed yet, and the framework match score is 0% demonstrated (up to 100% if unknown skills were met). This is not a hiring probability. To improve SQL, start with the recommended resources: PostgreSQL Tutorial [S1] and SQLBolt [S2]. Focus on completing guided tasks and practicing joins and aggregations. Once you have a baseline, you can move on to other required skills like Data Visualization and Data Wrangling.

items.answer: The information about other students' projects is not recorded in your profile or shared across the platform for privacy reasons. To build a project that aligns with your target role as a Data Analyst, focus on your skill gaps and choose a project that demonstrates multiple skills at once. For example, you could build a dashboard using a public dataset, which would involve data wrangling, SQL, and data visualization. You can find guidance on how to plan and execute such a project in the AI Career Guidance App [S1](#S1), [S2](#S2), and [S3](#S3). Start by identifying your highest-priority gaps and then break the project into manageable milestones.

items.question: Which learning resources should I use for my highest-priority gaps, and what should I do first?
sources: Planning portfolio projects that demonstrate skills
Effective learning strategies for technical skills
Effective learning strategies for technical skills
How the AI Career Guidance App works — methodology and limitations
Effective learning strategies for technical skills
items.answer:
For your highest-priority gaps, start by establishing a baseline for **SQL** and **Data Visualization**, as these are required at level 3 and are foundational for a Data Analyst role. Here's what you should do first:

- **SQL**: Begin with [PostgreSQL Tutorial](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/tutorial.html) or [SQLBolt](https://sqlbolt.com/). These resources will help you build a strong foundation in SQL, which is critical for data analysis.
- **Data Visualization**: Start with [Matplotlib Tutorials](https://matplotlib.org/stable/tutorials/index.html) or [Kaggle Learn: Data Visualization](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/data-visualization). These will introduce you to tools like Matplotlib and Tableau, which are essential for creating visual insights from data.

Once you have a baseline in these areas, focus on **Data Wrangling** using [pandas: Getting started](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/getting_started/index.html) or [Kaggle Learn: Pandas](https://www.kaggle.com/learn/pandas). These resources will help you learn how to clean and manipulate data effectively.

Remember to test your understanding by solving problems from memory or explaining concepts without notes, as this reinforces learning [S3]. Also, ensure the resources you use are up-to-date and relevant to current tools and practices [S5].
